display: Home cook from Kabul in Dandenong, cooking Afghan food for 50 to 200 people and trying to turn it into a registered catering business.

signals.text: I'm trying to turn my community cooking into a registered food business, but the licensing rules feel like a maze.
The council says I can't sell food cooked at home, so I need a registered commercial food premises.
Commercial kitchens in Dandenong cost $45 to $60 an hour, and I can't pay rent before I have paying customers.
I'm stuck in a loop: I can't get customers without selling, and I can't sell without a kitchen I can't afford.
I need to find out what a Class 3 food premises registration requires, including the kitchen layout and a food safety supervisor.
I'm taking the online food safety supervisor course on 25 October and want to be ready for the registration.
Many people in my community say they'd pay for my food if I had a shop, and I keep answering 'inshallah' because I can't say yes yet.
A school parent asked me to cook for her 74-year-old father, who has diabetes. I said yes and put off talking about payment until the licence is sorted.
I want to make Afghan food lighter, with less oil and salt, for people with heart or blood-sugar conditions.
I'm reading official English letters with a dictionary and would like someone to help me understand the regulatory language.
I'm studying for the citizenship test every night after the children sleep, and I want to book it for early November.
I'm worried about money and wouldn't risk the family savings on a kitchen rental before I know it will work.
I'm anxious and stretched thin, with a family member's immigration case dragging on while I'm trying to start the business.

offers.text: I cook Afghan food at scale for 50 to 200 people: mantu, qabuli pulao, bolani, ashak and aush.
I know about 300 families in the Afghan community in Dandenong and Springvale, and I cook for most of their weddings, Eid gatherings and fundraisers.
I hold a Level 2 food handler certificate.
I run a Facebook page with 1,100 followers and photos of my food.
I can write down recipes and price events in a spreadsheet.
I have my own equipment: two big pots, six trays and a stand mixer.
I know how to cook Afghan food low-salt and low-oil, without fried onions, because I cooked this way for years for a family member with a heart condition.
I can offer menu advice and recipes for school events and community groups that need food for different dietary needs.
I'm free to cook during school hours, 9 to 3 on weekdays, and on some weekends.
I can be a first, loyal customer for a shared commercial kitchen, with regular community orders already waiting.

catchers.hypo: Hi, I manage a commercial kitchen in the south-east. We have quiet weekday hours and would like to rent them cheaply to a new food business.
catchers.can: Zahra can book regular weekday cook sessions, bring in her existing community orders and show real demand within weeks.
catchers.confirm: Could the kitchen be booked in blocks of about six hours at a lower, flexible, or deferred rate?

catchers.hypo: I'm a food safety consultant. I help home cooks get a Class 3 registration and I've worked with this council.
catchers.can: Zahra can explain her situation and take advice on the kitchen layout, the supervisor requirement and the order of steps.
catchers.confirm: Do you have experience with Class 3 food premises applications in a Victorian council area, and do you offer free or low-cost help to small starters?

catchers.hypo: I run a community hall or social enterprise kitchen that's already registered, and we want local cooks to use it as an incubator.
catchers.can: Zahra can cook there under the existing registration while she builds up customers and her own application.
catchers.confirm: Is the kitchen already registered as a food premises that a separate small business can use under its own supervisor?

catchers.hypo: My father is 74 and has diabetes. I'm looking for home-style Afghan meals that fit his diet.
catchers.can: Zahra can cook light, low-salt, low-oil dishes through a friend's kitchen or after she's registered, and her community network can help the family.
catchers.confirm: Is the meal for a specific person with a health condition, and are you willing to wait until she's licensed before paying her?

catchers.hypo: I'm a dietitian or nurse. A patient's family wants culturally familiar food that still suits a heart or diabetes diet.
catchers.can: Zahra can adapt traditional Afghan dishes to the dietary guidance she's given and test them with families in her community.
catchers.confirm: Do you have a written dietary guideline she can follow, and would you be happy for her to cook from it rather than give medical advice?

catchers.hypo: I organise a school, mosque, or festival event and need halal Afghan food for a group of 50 to 200 people.
catchers.can: Zahra can quote and cook for large events using her recipes, spreadsheet pricing and her community's trust.
catchers.confirm: Is the event in Melbourne's south-east, with a date at least a few weeks away, and are you able to supply a registered or borrowed kitchen?

catchers.hypo: I help new arrivals understand Australian small-business rules, such as ABN, insurance, tax and council registration, and I'd like to work with someone who's just starting.
catchers.can: Zahra can describe her business, use the support, and pass the contact to other cooks in her community who face the same maze.
catchers.confirm: Do you offer this in plain English or Dari/Farsi, and is it free or low-cost for a very small start-up?

catchers.hypo: I'm an Afghan woman in Melbourne and I've been cooking for friends. I'd like to start selling too but don't know how.
catchers.can: Zahra can share what she's learned about the council's rules, and through her network of about 300 families she can pass along other women who cook.
catchers.confirm: Are you in the Dandenong or Springvale area, and would you be willing to share a kitchen booking or a learning group with other cooks?

catchers.hypo: I'm a volunteer teaching English or citizenship test preparation, and I'm looking for learners who study at night.
catchers.can: Zahra can join practice sessions, bring her friends and help others in her community who are preparing for the test.
catchers.confirm: Do you run sessions after 6 pm or at the local library, and do they cover the values and democracy questions?

catchers.hypo: I'm a school staff member planning a fundraiser or cultural day and want to include families' cooking in a way that meets food safety rules.
catchers.can: Zahra can cook for the stall, offer recipes children can help with, and bring bolani to share the culture.
catchers.confirm: Is this a one-off school event where food can be prepared in a permitted way, such as in the school kitchen or by a registered caterer?

forbids.text: I won't sell food cooked in my home kitchen, because the council doesn't allow it.
I can't pay commercial kitchen rent up front without customers or a deferred arrangement.
I'm not available to work during school pick-up and drop-off, so only 9 am to 3 pm on weekdays.
I'm not available for night shifts or work that takes me away from my children.
I don't give medical advice. I can cook to a diet that a doctor or dietitian gives me.
I won't use the family's savings for the business, because they're set aside for the children.

projects.name: Dandenong Afghan Kitchen
projects.text: A small registered catering business selling Afghan food for community events and weekend orders, starting with the events people already ask me to cook for.
roles_needed: Commercial kitchen owner or manager with spare hours
Food safety or council registration advisor
Dietitian to review light, low-salt dishes
Event organiser or first corporate and community customer

policy.t1: When a real collaboration looks possible, I'll share my licensing problem, my kitchen needs, my recipes and my experience cooking low-salt food for a family member with a heart condition.
policy.t2: Once I know who you are and the fit is strong, I'll share household finances and my family's immigration situation.
policy.never: Passport numbers, and details of my family's journey to Australia.
